long.title: 1816: The Year Summer Never Came
long.description:
Have you ever wondered how a mountain exploding on a tropical island could make it snow in July, half a world away? This is the story that has haunted me ever since I first heard it.

In April 1815, Mount Tambora erupted with the loudest sound in recorded human history, erasing two kingdoms and even a language. A year later, its ash veiled the sun, crops failed across the globe, and in a darkened Swiss villa, an eighteen-year-old girl dreamed of a monster called Frankenstein.

1:35 The Mountain That Roared
3:27 A Kingdom Erased

9:50 Echoes

shorts.title: The Loudest Sound in History #shorts #history #documentary
shorts.description:
Mount Tambora's 1815 eruption was heard 2,600 kilometers away. To this day, it remains the loudest sound in recorded human history.

shorts.title: A Volcano Invented Frankenstein #shorts #history #documentary
shorts.description:
A volcano darkened the sun in 1816, and in the gloom of Lake Geneva, Mary Shelley dreamed of a monster. Frankenstein was born from a volcanic winter.
